ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening per FINTRAC and OSFI standards, OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, and Canadian sanctions lists

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended — ss. 5-7 (incorporation and issuance of certificate of incorporation), s. 19 (registered office), s. 101 ff. (directors), s. 103 (by-laws), s. 113 (notice of directors); Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512 (fee tariff).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), 235 Queen Street, Ottawa, Ontario K1A 0H5; online filing centre at www.ic.gc.ca/corporations and My Business Account portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) filed electronically, issued with Integrated Statutory Notices — Initial Notice of Registered Office (Form 4003) and Notice of Directors (Form 4006); certificate of incorporation issued under CBCA s. 7.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow deposit rule under the CBCA; incorporation may proceed with nominal or deferred capital, provided at least one share is subscribed. Consideration may be cash, property, or past services. Non-resident ownership is unrestricted, subject to Investment Canada Act notification for a retail business where enterprise value exceeds the CAD 5 million threshold.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION: WHEREAS [Name] Inc. was incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act; RESOLVED THAT: 1. The Corporation accepts the incorporation subscription of [Subscriber], and the board allots and issues [•] common shares as fully paid upon receipt of CAD $[•] in cash. 2. The registered office is established at [Full Street Address], [City], Ontario, and the Initial Notice of Registered Office is approved for filing. 3. The following are appointed: [Name] — President; [Name] — Secretary; [Name] — Treasurer. 4. The President and Secretary are authorized to execute all filings and banking resolutions giving effect to the foregoing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Pre-Incorporation Name Search and Distinctiveness Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada — Online Filing Centre, NUANS name reservation; www.ic.gc.ca/corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File one proposed corporate name (e.g., '[Brand] Cosmetics Canada Inc.') to obtain a Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search (NUANS) report. Ensure the name is distinctive, does not suggest government association, and includes the legal element 'Inc.' or 'Corp.' as required by the CBCA. A numbered company (e.g., '1234567 Canada Inc.') may be elected without a NUANS search; a later change of name under CBCA s. 8 may add the trade name.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with legal element
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report discloses confusing similarity, revise the distinctive word element and re-run the search; alternatively incorporate under a numbered name and file a CBCA s. 8 change-of-name after trademark clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada — Online Filing Centre / My Business Account portal (ISED)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 4001 and file electronically: authorize share capital (e.g., unlimited Common shares without par value, optionally split into Class A Common and Class B Preferred for future investors), designate the registered office jurisdiction (Ontario recommended), and set the number of directors. Sign digitally via the incorporator's credential, pay the CAD 200.00 federal fee by credit card, and obtain issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, ordinarily within two business days of intake.
required_dossiers: Director information including resident Canadian status and residential addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On issuance of a deficiency notice by the Office of the Director, correct the flagged clause (share rights, director residency, or registered office) and resubmit within the prescribed correction window; a timely corrected filing preserves the original filing date and generally avoids a second fee.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must register with CRA to obtain a Business Number (BN) if carrying on business in Canada or maintaining a permanent establishment; Canadian corporations automatically receive BN upon incorporation under federal or provincial law via the online CRA My Business Account portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available under Canadian law; hybrid mismatch rules governed by GAAR and specific elections for foreign affiliate transactions under the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual taxable supplies in Canada
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: GST/HST registrants required to file returns and remit tax electronically via My Business Account; digital filing mandatory with no real-time fiscal clearance or API stamping obligations, though large registrants may use CRA APIs for transaction data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Canada qualify for 0% GST rate if not consumed in Canada and export is evidenced; digital services zero-rated when supplied to non-residents outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent shipping document
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or proof of payment from non-resident
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Failure to substantiate zero-rating triggers GST reassessment, interest charges, and penalties up to 200% of the tax amount for fraudulent claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in conjunction with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for banking prudential oversight; financial intelligence and AML/ATF supervision is vested in the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada does not operate a separate foreign exchange control administration or exchange surrender authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully and freely convertible on both current-account and capital-account basis under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no exchange controls, no prior approval for inbound portfolio or direct investment, and no restrictions on dividend distributions, management fees, royalty payments, or repatriation of paid-up capital by a federally incorporated Canada Business Corporation (CBCA corporation). Canadian withholding tax at 25% on non-resident payments, reduced by treaty, is administered under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act and does not constitute a convertibility or remittance barrier. FINTRAC reporting thresholds apply to currency and virtual currency transactions, but do not impose exchange control licensing. The legal currency remains legal tender but banks are free to price and settle transactions in any currency. Profit remittance through a Schedule I bank is executed as a routine FOREX transaction using standard settlement rails and requires only ordinary banking instructions plus the applicable tax compliance attestations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement. There is no mandatory conversion ratio, no prescribed timeline for repatriating export receipts, and no Central Bank custodian mechanism for export earnings. Cosmetic and beauty retailers operating as Canadian federal corporations are free to retain foreign currency proceeds in domestic or offshore settlement accounts, subject to general record-keeping under the Income Tax Act and to FINTRAC's 'large transaction' and 'financial entity' reporting obligations for transactions over CAD 10,000. For inbound e-commerce settlement via Shopify Payments or PayPal, funds may be pooled abroad and swept to a Canadian operating account without any exchange control filing, although banks may apply internal anti-money-laundering hold periods for new client relationships.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for foreign-domiciled electronic money institutions (EMIs) and non-bank payment service providers. Wise, Payoneer, and similar regulated e-money platforms are usable for merchant settlement and vendor disbursements but are not licensed as banks in Canada. They generally cannot accept deposits in Canada without registration under the Retail Payment Activities Act and oversight by the Bank of Canada and FINTRAC. Offshore EMIs that are not Canadian-registered may only provide inbound remittances and outbound transfers on a pass-through processing basis; they are not viable substitutes for a payments schedule and cannot hold Canadian operational funds as a licensed deposit-taker. It is recommended to maintain a Schedule I bank account as the primary liquidity anchor and use EMIs only for settlement optimization. Shopify Payments and PayPal are treated as merchant acquiring payment rails and are compatible with Schedule I account structures.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no federal statutory mandate under the Canada Business Corporations Act requiring physical attendance by directors for general corporate banking onboarding. However, the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and associated FINTRAC regulations require financial entities to apply a risk-based client identification regime. In practice, Schedule I banks permit remote account opening for a CBCA-incorporated corporation using attested corporate records, proof of registered office, director and shareholder certifications, and identity verification of directors and beneficial owners via video call, digital notarization, or third-party identity verification providers. All directors may be non-resident, and banks accept non-resident directors and foreign beneficial owners provided that enhanced due diligence is satisfied. Physical attendance may be requested only on a discretionary risk basis for unusual beneficial ownership structures or sanctions-related screening triggers; a prepared remote documentary package with full corporate registry extracts, certificate of good standing, notarized resolutions, and source-of-wealth memoranda typically eliminates the interview requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign resident director or controlling shareholder dwelling in a non-common-law jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passport, background and adverse-media search report, certified board resolutions, tax residency certificate, source of funds declaration with bank statements from originating jurisdiction, and a legal opinion on beneficial ownership in the corporate registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry coding mismatch or unexplained e-commerce revenue velocity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business registration, merchant processing agreements from Shopify Payments and PayPal, marketplace seller dashboard extraction, inventory purchase invoices, logistics service agreements, and a 12-month revenue projection with merchant clearing reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner with high wealth but no prior Canadian banking relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent source-of-wealth report, professionally prepared net-worth statement, asset ownership proofs, tax references, and a notarized declaration of ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a jurisdiction of concern for sanctions or terrorist financing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening from Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, legal counsel confirmation of license exception or exemption, chain-of-funds on the convertible currency transfer, and OSFI-compliant enhanced due diligence questionnaire for the remitting financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Physical mailbox only and virtual office as corporate registered address
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Federal incorporation certificate, annual return filing receipt, registered office address record with Corporations Canada, list of records-directed physical service location, and attestation by corporate counsel that the virtual office is lawfully maintained.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital and operational funds uses SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic transfers through a Canadian Schedule I bank correspondent network. Common ancillary SWIFT fields should be accurately coded: complete legal name of the CBCA corporation, Toronto or registered provincial address, federal jurisdiction, and any partnership with the ultimate shareholder reference. Canadian banks do not apply exchange controls, but they must screen against Global Affairs Canada sanctions, FINTRAC reporting, and OSFI anti-money-laundering directives. For tax purposes, inbound capital contributions should be designated as paid-up share capital or shareholder loan, not as trading revenue; the bank requires an account-purpose declaration and the client must record the funds in the corporate treasury system as 'capital injection', not 'sales proceeds'. Attention is required to SWIFT purpose-of-payment fields that reference 'foreign direct investment' or 'capital subscription' to ensure accurate filing of the Government of Canada's balance-of-payments reports through the Bank of Canada's statistical reporting system. Real-time domestic clearing via Lynx (large-value transfer system) is available for CAD-denominated domestic concentration from merchant acquirers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for procurement of cosmetics inventory, packaging components, and international logistics are cleared via standard commercial payment instruments: SWIFT MT103 for irrevocable international wire transfers; clean collection (MT400/MT210) where no documentary credit is required; SWIFT MT700 issuance of an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit for high-value bulk raw-material purchases; and MT707 amendments or MT740 authorization when necessary. For low-value recurring disbursements, the automated clearing settlement system via Payments Canada's Real-Time Rail (RTR) and pre-authorized electronic funds transfers (EFT) in CAD is permitted, but international trade payments should consistently use SWIFT to preserve audit trails and correspondent-bank exchange rate certainty. Payment instruction packages should include the tax invoices, incoterms, proof of export, and customs declarations, because Canadian banks conduct post-transaction sanctions screening and enhanced due diligence on the cargo description. For retail-oriented inbound business, Shopify Payments can be used for customer refunds and supplier disbursements within Canada, while cross-border inventory settlement should be channeled through the Schedule I bank treasury desk to manage FOREX and regulatory reporting holistically.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Entering into deliverable FX spot and forward contracts (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/CNY) with a Schedule I bank treasury as permissible OTC hedging products, with confirmation under ISDA or Canadian Bankers Association master agreements.

Non-deliverable forward contracts for specific currencies for which convertibility may be limited in the counterparty jurisdiction, executed as offshore NDFs through Canadian Schedule I bank dealing desks, with underlying exposure to Chinese renminbi and certain Asian settlement currencies.
Cross-currency basis swaps and plain-vanilla currency swaps between CAD and USD or CAD and EUR, accessibly to the treasury for matching long-term sales and procurement currency exposures.
Plain-vanilla FX options and collars under the same treasury mandate for managing volatility around seasonal promotional cycles, subject to board approval and prudent risk management policies.
Futures and listed options on CAD/USD traded on North American exchanges (e.g., CME Group) as exchange-traded linear instruments when OTC counterparty credit limits are absent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under section 263 of the Canada Business Corporations Act, including current registered office address, directors, and corporate particulars.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary date of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuation under the CBCA.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A default notice is issued after the annual return becomes overdue. Continued failure for two consecutive annual return periods permits the Director under CBCA section 212 to dissolve the corporation administratively. Reinstatement requires a revival application, payment of outstanding annual return fees, and applicable remedial fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and supporting CRA schedules under the Income Tax Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's taxation year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% for each complete month of delay, up to 12 months. Repeated late filings may trigger an increased penalty, and compound daily interest applies to unpaid balances and balance-due amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return where the corporation is a registrant and qualifies for annual filing under the Excise Tax Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year for annual filers; GST/HST registration is mandatory once taxable supplies exceed C$30,000 in a calendar quarter or in a trailing four-quarter period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or remit triggers late-filing penalties under the Excise Tax Act, including monthly arrears penalties up to 12 months, compound daily interest, and potential director liability for unremitted amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4/T4SUM Payroll Information Return, only where the corporation has employees.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of February following the calendar year in which employee remuneration was paid, subject to CRA electronic filing extension rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties are assessed per T4 slip for late submission, failure to provide employee copies, and failure to remit source deductions; director liability may apply to unremitted employee income tax, CPP, and EI amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No CBCA revenue or asset threshold triggers an audit. A non-distributing corporation may dispense with an auditor only by unanimous shareholder consent for each financial year. Absent that unanimous waiver, an auditor must be appointed irrespective of entity size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises; private corporations may use IFRS or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), both forming Canadian GAAP under the CPA Canada Handbook.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO return is filed with Corporations Canada. Under the CBCA, the corporation must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control and update it within 15 days after becoming aware of any change, including changes resulting from shareholding transfers. Management should perform an annual confirmation review before the shareholders' meeting and verify that the ISC register reflects current ownership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 to 440 per year for a standard Canadian registered office and records address; broader corporate secretarial support commonly ranges from USD 750 to 1,850 per year.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 to 25,000 for a full statutory audit of a small e-commerce entity; review engagement USD 2,500 to 6,000; nil when audit is waived by unanimous shareholder consent.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal Part I general corporate rate (38% basic rate minus 10% provincial abatement minus 13% general rate reduction). Provincial and territorial corporate rates (8.4%-16%) produce a combined statutory rate of approximately 23%-31%, depending on permanent establishment allocation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CCPC Small Business Deduction (ITA s.125) reduces federal rate to 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, phased out when taxable capital employed in Canada exceeds CAD 10M (fully at CAD 50M) and when adjusted aggregate investment income exceeds CAD 50,000. SR&ED refundable investment tax credit of 35% for CCPCs on the first CAD 3M of qualified expenditure (15% non-refundable above), applicable to cosmetics formulation and proprietary e-commerce development. Additional incentives: immediate expensing of eligible capital property (Class 44?; CCA Classes 50/53/54), 100% CCA on eligible computer equipment? and input tax credits for GST/HST on business inputs.
corporate_income_tax_regime.loss_carryforward_regime: Non-capital losses may be carried back 3 taxation years and forward 20 taxation years (ITA s.111(1)(a)); net capital losses of a corporation may be carried back 3 years and forward 5 years (s.111(1)(b)). Losses of a federal corporation arising in the DTC cosmetics retailing business are ordinary non-capital losses and carry forward 20 years.
